query: Big Tech M&A activity 2026 pace, record $10B+ deals, and antitrust environment for large tech acquisitions in 2026
answer:
I've completed comprehensive research on Big Tech M&A activity in 2026. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Summary

**Pace (record value, falling volume):** H1 2026 hit ~$2.8 trillion in global M&A (up 48% YoY, the highest first-half on record since 1980), even as deal count fell ~9% to a six-year low. Full-year 2026 is on track for ~$4 trillion (PwC) — the strongest since 2021. The defining pattern is "fewer deals, bigger stakes."

**Record $10B+ deals:** 47 mega-deals of $10B+ in H1 2026, worth over $1.3 trillion combined and accounting for nearly 50% of all global deal volume — an all-time record concentration. Six deals exceeded $50B. Largest: Paramount–Warner Bros (~$170B), NextEra–Dominion (~$66.8B), SpaceX–Cursor (~$60B, AI), PIF/Silver Lake–EA (~$55B).

**Tech-specific:** Technology led all sectors at ~$649B in H1; EY reports Q2 tech deal value doubled YoY. Roughly half of tech deals are AI-adjacent. Notably, Big Tech's dominant AI spending is *organic capex* (~$650–725B combined for the four hyperscalers), not acquisitions — partly because antitrust scrutiny pushes them toward acqui-hires/licensing.

**Antitrust environment:** Described as "more permissive/friendlier" toward mergers under Trump's FTC (Ferguson) and DOJ (Slater), favoring negotiated remedies over litigation — but the Biden-era 2023 Merger Guidelines and stricter HSR rules remain in effect. Q1 2026 saw only 4 significant US merger investigations (avg 10.8 months, no contested complaints). However, Big Tech remains the top priority on *monopolization conduct* (ongoing Google/Meta/Amazon/Apple cases), and AI consolidation is scrutinized. The EU is similarly permissive on merger volume (decade-low investigations) while assertive on digital conduct.

All findings are cited with sources and quantitative data points in the structured output.
